items.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: And I play with James Moody, he’s 76 now, he’s playing better than ever.

ctx.x: Yeah, then all of a sudden you’re elevated to this status and you’re just like almost a beginner in the field.

Right, yeah. And that whole mentoring situation doesn’t seem to be existing that much now. And I mean I remember when I was always the young guy in the band. I was always the baby. And now I’m in certain situations where I’m the old man, but then I’m still in © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

situations where I am the young guy. And I play with James Moody, he’s 76 now, he’s playing better than ever. And you know it, I don’t even think he has a record deal now, and he’s one of the real icons of the music, and one of the last of the survivors and he’s at the peak of his game, and he doesn’t even have a deal now. Because I think he was with a big company and they were saying well we want you to do this, we want you to do that.
